title: Animation Throwdown: The Quest for Cards
text: 100% Pay to Win. I've played this game for many many hours on my phone before it came to steam. all in all its fun for a while...  until you hit the enevitable pay wall known as Secret Fight Club (SFC). The PVP aspect of this game doesnt determine if you have skill, it only calculates your power rating and pits you against 3 players you can beat easily, then places you against a player that has dumped a lot of coin on this game (known as Whales) that you simply cannot compete with. to reiterate once you make it to SFC and plateau at a rating your win loss cycle will go exactly like this: win, win, win, loss, loss, win, loss, loss, loss, win. which after you complete the cycle will place your rating at slightly lower than where you started. rinse and repeat. this is exactly what will happen. When i started playing the game, it seemed to have a very linear, and less pay to win outlook. Card combos were quite finite and gave the impression that in the long run you could obtain all the cards necessary for a very padded deck, just from playing. But fast foward to about the time that this game made it on to steam, the devs did something to change the dynamic and meta of the game. They started churning out NEW Legendary and Epics every month, which you need 4 of to max out combos. And they seem to add 12 to 20 new cards Every month now. Oh yeah, they also added Pre-Combo'ed Power Cards, which have even higher stats, and are for the most part useless if you only have one of each, you need a dual combo to make them even somewhat relevant. Sure at low levels these cards are a great boost on their own, but once you make it into SFC, single Legendaries and Power Cards just wont cut it. Quad Fused Epics too are mostly useless once you hit SFC... but unless you dump cash for Legendaries your deck will be mostly comprised of Quad Fused Epics, which work ok until you come across a Whale that has Quad fused Legendary everything. Add to that the Mythic level cards, which have the highest level stats, which you can buy for literally $200 each (cheap right?), or grind out challenge coins for having a less than .0001% for each super epic pack to produce one. (Seriously knives in CSGO drop more frequently).  That glimmer of having a decently padded deck in due time has now faded, and this game has clearly shown its true nature: Buy cards and win, or sit and stagnate for months with little to no progression of deck development. But with the addition of new cards Every month, there is increasing smaller chance to have maxed out legendaries, because the pool of cards is continuing to increase in size. which is really a problem because you simply cannot progress or compete in SFC without having legendaries combo'd to the max. Unless of course you want to drop $100 each time they whip out a new card pack (2x a month) and even then, there is no guarantee you will get enough good cards to make max combos. There are literally guys that have spent thousands of dollars building their deck, and those are the whales sitting at the very top of the leaderboards, and you will not even get close to approaching that level unless you too dump thousands of dollars. this is very real, and not an exageration. The steam version also trims out the "Ad Bonus" that is available to phone users, this adds a multiplier to your winnings in Adventure and Arena modes, which without this multiplier makes the rewards useless.  non-existant on steam Unless you pay $10 per WEEK for just the multiplier bonus. To further insult to injury, on the mobile version, on occasion you will receive an "Ad Bonus Crate" (completely absent from the Steam version) which is just an on-demand advert, but you get decent *cough* rewards for watching it. The rewards have 4 tiers, the lowest gives you 500 coins and 5 more adventure energy, the next level 1000 coins and 5 adventure and arena energy, 1500 coins and 10 adventure and 10 arena energy. and the highest 2000 coins, 10 energy to aventure and arena, but also will drop a random card, from rare to legendary. The added bonus energy points are necessary to compete in any of the weekly competitions in arena, or you get stuck with just minimal points/rewards. These features are also pay to win, as you are paying your time for their ad revenue profit. the trade off is more adventure and arena time. which translates to more cards and possible competition winnings. I have regretably dropped around $60 over time on this game, and that has only left me with a mediocre deck with only 8 dual fused legendaries (you need four for max combo) single legendaries are pretty much useless. granted i can do ok at my rank in SFC (stuck at around 1000) but there is no progression, and I actually believe that over time if the current modus operandi of churning out new cards every month continues then you will actually lose rank in SFC unless you start dumping cash on this greed machine.

text: Despite hints of its pay-to-win nature, I initially felt I’d been a little too harsh on the game after completing my first impressions video. Then I played for a couple more hours….. At this point I was locked out of all the game modes apart from practice. I either had to purchase more energy or wait a number of real-world hours. (My first impressions video) The pay to win rears it's head when you’ve played for a couple of hours and have access to research. Research lets you create combo cards (the games only interesting mechanic which they’ve ruined) but you have to wait 8 hours for them to complete. You can pay real money to speed up the process. Combo cards are powerful and usually take 2 turns to play. Researching a combo card lets you drop it in one turn. This lessens the RNG when playing and means if you get a decent combo card down early you’re likely to win, until you reach a player with a better combo card or a higher level character. This game is not skill based that's for sure. You can also upgrade cards to make them more powerful and all of this can be done more quickly with real money. Hence, the more you pay, the more likely you are to win. This game is after your cash, nothing more. Steam is flushed with free CCGs at the moment and a lot of them are not only far superior games, they have a fair fairer business model too. Stay away.

title: Anomaly: Warzone Earth
text: Why play a Tower Defence game, when you can play a Tower ATTACK game?! Anomaly: Warzone Earth truly throws the Tower Defence genre upside-down. The player indirectly controls a wave of units, designating the path and using support abilities to protect the units as they advance. This is an easy game to adapt to and only covers a few basic strategies, but continues to challenge the player as new units, abilities and enemies are introduced throughout the game. The graphical engine is impressive, well polished and looks excellent. This game can be completed in just under 10 hours. Although a high-score system is present throughout the game, the basic mechanics of the game diminish the games replay value. Overall, this is a really impressive indie game to come out of a small Polish development team.

title: Anomaly: Warzone Earth
text: 8/10 Turret attack is a comparatively rare genre. Turret attack done well is even more so. title: Antenna
text: The Buzzer speaks, and we are bound to listen Ever wonder what it was like to listen to the tunes and programs on the old radios, before the advent of the internet and digital technology? When radio-waves were able to change to course of the history? When they reigned supreme? Wonder no longer and enjoy this short and brilliant puzzle adventure called “Antenna”, a love letter to radio waves and transmissions packed in an elegant and minimalistic style. Visually, Antenna borrows a lot of the look and style of the Limbo game with the black and white, clean and surreal feel that will keep you glued to the screen from start till end. There are no excessive details or visual effects in the game that would distract from keeping an eye and ear out to everything that is happening at the screen. The minimalistic style of the game successfully conveys the feeling of cold, machine-like precision and mystery that surrounds the Antenna’s levels. Sound is the second equally important part of the game, with luscious and enigmatic sounds and transmissions the player will have to focus on in order to solve a few of the Antenna’s well implemented and interesting puzzles. The only gripe that I have is that it ends too soon, you will barely need more than 30 minutes to finish the game, with only a handful of well-designed sound puzzles it offers. I definitely recommend Antenna to anyone who wants to try something different and strange, a mystery that is open to interpretation, with adept look and sound to match, and I hope the developers will one day create a full-fledged game out of this idea, telling many more stories of the monolithic effect analogue sounds and radio waves held over people in the past, and still continue to do, in the shroud of secrecy.

title: Antisquad
text: What the Hell is Antisquad? Well it's a turn base tactical action game, similar to Jagged Alliance, Shadow Run, X-Com Serie, Commandos, Desperados.... You are in command of a small team of Mercs, (Military Special Force, Expendables, No Lifers... whatever) send to clean the world infested with baddies, gangsters, cartel drug dealers, criminals, terrorists, WMD users and other Nutters that threaten our peacefull planet. (damn scumbags) At your disposal, you have a wide range of gears and weapons that you can use to perform your missions, as long as you have enough money to buy them, money that you'll earn from killing baddies, acconplishing challenges, keeping your team alive.... Each of your character has a specific set of skills so select your team carefully before you start your mission. The game has a simple storyline, missions are to: kill this, go there, push this, kill more, nuke end boss, go to next stage, buy gears, upgrade characters..a feeling of 'deja vu'. However, Antisquad is a really enjoyable game and makes it up with nice graphics where the characters kinda look like in TF2, a good atmospheric soundtrack short but brutal and bloody missions with some nice surprises along the way. Antisquad will not win the Tactical Game of the year but it SURE will give you tonnes of fun time and hours spend trying to complet the long list of Achievements and challenges. title: Antisquad
text: Reasonably impressed thus far. Antisquad is a no-frills turn based strategy which takes the genre back to basics, while still encouraging players to think tactically. Antisquad's combat focuses on line of sight rather than cover, and players many times need to sneak carefully around in order to avoid pulling dozens of mobs on accident. It can be deliciously tense when things go wrong, but there are balance issues. Being in alpha, there are characters who are massively OP compared to their counterparts. Scouts, for example, can move almost the range of the entire map, attack multiple times, and still take a few rounds of damage before they go down. This creates a problem as the game has many characters to be enjoyed, but playing optimally is often a matter of forgoing frontline combatants and taking only scouts / snipers. Still, different characters synergize well together, and can be a joy to play depending on your group composition. A huge amount of gear and upgrades are available for each character which change both their attributes and appearance, giving the game a huge density of content for the price you pay. Definitely worth watching.

title: Aquaria
text: So, I played the game and got to a certain point and then all my data got deleted. Not an issue since I really liked this game alot. I started over and got better at it, decided to explore further and so far I love the boss battles and the fact you can shoot all the creatures of this world. It's a very visually stunning game and has a feel like a Underwater Metroidvania/Shoot-Em-Up genre. I got stuck and read a walkthrough, seems like I'm close to finishing the game so it might be a short game, but I'm not so sure. I'm hoping it's longer as I may edit my review later. But so far it's Great! *UPDATE* So turns out I wasn't close to the ending at all. Had alot of areas I haven't explored and took a very long time to beat the game. I think 30 hours respectively to finally beat the game.  I've got to say... This game is one of my personal favorites! I love the story, I love the game play and I love everything about it! Farming for ingredients for recipes gaining different forms and abilities really took me back to my Super Metroid Days! The bosses were all fun and challenging, the creatures you encounter in different ecosystems and the hidden treasures and costumes you can find. For those of you wondering if you should buy this game and what it's about, take the game Ecco for the Sega Genesis and Metroid for the Nintendo and you got yourself Aquaria! I'm really looking forward to the next chapter if BitBlot decides to continue the story.
